summary: U.S. equities posted modest gains Friday to cap a volatile week dominated by Treasury market turbulence and a historic cryptocurrency rally. The S&P 500 climbed 0.43% to 7,674, while the Dow added nearly 1% despite weekly losses across major indices driven by a bond sell-off that pressured risk assets. Bitcoin surged to $77,000, recording its best week in two years with a 22% gain, fueled by President Trump's push for the CLARITY Act and the Treasury's announcement to double long-term debt buybacks. The crypto-friendly regulatory shift sparked a dramatic rally in digital assets and related equities, with Robinhood jumping 14% and Coinbase up 8%. Meanwhile, business activity data showed U.S. expansion at its fastest pace in over four years, and all eyes now turn to Nvidia's Wednesday earnings report, which could determine tech's next move after the Nasdaq 100 halted a five-day losing streak.

signals.title: Bitcoin rallies 22% on Trump's CLARITY Act push and Treasury buyback plan
signals.desc: Bitcoin hit $77,000 in its best week since 2024 as Trump urged Congress to pass crypto legislation and Treasury announced doubled long-term debt repurchases, injecting liquidity and suppressing yields.

signals.title: U.S. business activity expands at fastest pace in four years
signals.desc: Strong PMI data supported equity gains Friday and reduced near-term recession fears, though bond yields remain elevated following week-long Treasury volatility.

signals.title: Nvidia earnings Wednesday could decide tech sector direction
signals.desc: Wall Street expects 99% YoY earnings growth to $2.09 per share on $92B revenue, with AI demand and hyperscaler capex plans in focus as Nasdaq 100 sits at key technical levels.

signals.title: Crypto-related stocks surge on regulatory optimism
signals.desc: Robinhood rallied 14% and Coinbase gained 8% Friday as bitcoin's 22% weekly advance and Trump's crypto legislation push boosted sentiment for digital asset platforms.

signals.title: Major indices post weekly losses despite Friday bounce
signals.desc: S&P 500 fell 1.4% for the week and tech shed 3% over five days as rising Treasury yields and bond market volatility pressured growth stocks, particularly in semiconductors.

verdict: Crypto's historic rally and solid macro data provide near-term support, but Treasury volatility and Nvidia's Wednesday print will determine whether risk appetite holds or fades.
